stop_status: CLEAR after repair. One allocator-seam error coordinate was wrong (L_STRNDUP 175 vs the pinned authority's 197), one signed-overflow edge in the operation loop was removed, and one misleading contract comment was corrected. No confirmed memory-safety defect, no ABI regression, no weakened detector, no new hidden obligation and no new production unsafe operation. Nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE.

authority.source: openssl-3.6.4 crypto/core_algorithm.c, sha256 182f4a8da3bb320edcab1ed94f2cb16f3956bd1768e451ae3cedc4e8cb26bb85, 6246 bytes; compared whole against src/evp/algorithm.rs (algorithm_do_map, algorithm_do_this, ossl_algorithm_do_all, ossl_algorithm_get1_first_name).
authority.abi: No export, signature, #[repr(C)] layout or unsafe lint attribute changed. ossl_algorithm_do_all and ossl_algorithm_get1_first_name remain pub(crate) without #[no_mangle]; AlgorithmData remains a Rust-only stack structure; the OsslAlgorithm four-pointer layout and all five callback typedefs are unchanged.
external_contracts: A provider's query_operation answer is NULL or a NULL-algorithm_names-terminated OSSL_ALGORITHM array; every non-terminator row's algorithm_names is a NUL-terminated ':'-separated alias list. The provider keeps the array valid until the matching unquery_operation.

ossl_provider_doall_activated takes a reference and raises the activation count on every already-activated provider under the store/flag locks, invokes the callback outside every lock, and undoes both afterwards. algorithm_do_this therefore runs with a live, pinned provider and holds no registry lock.

reserve_store, fn_ and unreserve_store are non-NULL; pre and post are optional. api_do_map calls reserve_store once per map and pairs it with unreserve_store on every exit after a successful reserve, including both failure arms.

A refused precondition (pre returns non-zero with result = 0) is success and skips the map; a pre error (returns 0) is -1; a post that returns 0 overwrites ret with -1. These three conventions are observable and are pinned by tests.

The callback lock discipline belongs to the callback implementations: method_store's reserve_store takes the method-store lock and holds it across pre, every fn_ and post; those callbacks must not re-enter that store lock. This file takes no lock of its own.

operation_id is 0 (every operation) or an id in OSSL_OP_DIGEST..=OSSL_OP_HIGHEST (1..=22). The authority's for-loop overflows a signed int for INT_MAX; the crate's checked increment terminates instead.

boundaries.mechanism: ossl_algorithm_do_all entry, AlgorithmData stack lifetime, provider selection and libctx rewrite
boundaries.contract: libctx NULL or live; provider NULL or live; reserve_store/fn_/unreserve_store non-NULL; pre/post NULL or valid; data opaque and passed back unchanged; operation_id 0 or 1..=22. cbdata is this frame's live stack object and cbptr is passed only to the synchronous doall/do_this call. The no-provider path sweeps activated providers (which doall pins); the named path requires the caller to keep provider alive, compares concrete contexts, and silently returns on mismatch (non-fatal ossl_assert parity).

boundaries.mechanism: algorithm_do_this per-provider operation walk and query/unquery pairing
boundaries.contract: provider live and cbdata a live AlgorithmData. Each operation is query_operation -> algorithm_do_map -> unquery_operation, including when the query answers NULL; the array is provider-owned until unquery. A hard -1 returns 0 immediately, a soft 0 sets ok = 0 and continues. The operation increment is checked, so the loop always terminates and no signed overflow can cross the unsafe extern "C" boundary.

boundaries.mechanism: algorithm_do_map callback sequence: reserve_store, pre, per-entry fn_, post, unreserve_store
boundaries.contract: provider live for every callback implementation; map NULL or terminated; cbdata live. reserve_store is called unconditionally and, when it answers non-zero, unreserve_store is called on every exit path. A refused precondition becomes success and skips the map; a pre error is -1 with no post; a post returning 0 overwrites ret with -1. fn_ runs once per non-terminator row. This function holds no lock and allocates nothing.

algo is a live OSSL_ALGORITHM whose algorithm_names is NULL or a NUL-terminated ':'-separated list. NULL answers NULL without allocating; otherwise the first colon (or the whole string) is copied with CRYPTO_strndup at the pinned authority coordinate crypto/core_algorithm.c:197 and the fresh block is transferred to the caller, which releases it once. The function never releases it.

boundaries.mechanism: registry serialization and callback reentrancy edge (reused B9/B10 contract)
boundaries.contract: The activated-provider sweep takes references and raises activation counts under the store/flag locks and invokes algorithm_do_this with no lock held; query/unquery bracket the whole map walk; the only lock held across pre/fn_/post is the method-store lock the caller's reserve_store takes. The resulting order is method-store lock -> provider opbits lock (pre/post), matching the authority.

defects.description: L_STRNDUP was 175, which is the named-provider path's `return;` in the pinned authority, not the OPENSSL_strndup call. The value reaches CRYPTO_strndup as the file/line recorded on an allocation failure, so the authority seam coordinate was wrong.
defects.fix: L_STRNDUP is now 197, the pinned authority's `ret = OPENSSL_strndup(algo->algorithm_names, first_name_len);`. FILE was already the authority's ../../src/openssl-3.6.4/ spelling and is unchanged.

defects.description: cur_operation += 1 in algorithm_do_this overflows when operation_id is INT_MAX: a debug build panics across an unsafe extern "C" function, and a release build wraps and walks an effectively unbounded range. The C authority's for-loop has the same signed-integer overflow, which is UB.
defects.fix: The increment is cur_operation.checked_add(1) with a defined break on overflow. Every valid operation id (0 or 1..=22) takes exactly the authority's path; the out-of-contract id now stops instead of reproducing the authority's UB. The contract now names the valid domain.

defects.description: The comment on the named-provider libctx rewrite claimed the field was read through cbptr and that every callback saw it. In the authority and the crate cbdata.libctx is written and never read: callbacks receive the caller's separate `data` pointer. The claim implied a reader and could mislead a reentrancy review.
defects.fix: The comment now states authority parity: the field is written for fidelity and has no reader; the allow(unused_assignments) is explained accordingly.

The full library suite was run twice on the final blob, with --test-threads=1 and --test-threads=4, so the module's global callback fixtures were exercised under both execution schedules.

The allocator seam coordinate was checked against the pinned authority blob (sha256 182f4a8d..., 6246 bytes), which places OPENSSL_strndup at line 197. No production test allocates through ossl_algorithm_get1_first_name, so the coordinate correction has a source witness rather than a runtime allocation-failure control.

residuals.disposition: RECORDED external provider contract - authority parity
residuals.description: The OSSL_ALGORITHM array and every algorithm_names list are provider-owned. A malformed provider table (missing NULL terminator or NUL) would be over-read by the walk/first-name scan exactly as the authority's loop/strchr would. Terminating the array and NUL-terminating names is the provider ABI's obligation; the array must stay valid until unquery_operation.

The caller's reserve_store commonly takes a non-reentrant method-store lock and this file holds it across pre, every fn_ and post. Those callbacks must not re-enter that store lock; lock order is method-store -> provider opbits. The discipline is method_store's contract (audited separately), reused here unchanged.

residuals.disposition: RECORDED authority hazard - not reproduced as a panic
residuals.description: operation_id outside 0 or 1..=22 is outside the contract. The authority's loop overflows for INT_MAX; the checked increment now stops. Negative ids query once and stop, which is the authority's non-overflowing natural behaviour.

The named-provider path's concrete-context assertion is non-fatal under NDEBUG, so a caller mismatch is a silent no-walk. This is deliberate parity; the function still requires provider to be live and held for the duration of the direct walk.

cbdata.libctx is written on the named-provider path and never read by this file; the callbacks receive the caller's separate opaque `data`. The write is retained for fidelity and is documented as dead rather than presented as a live callback input.
